headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default data-leak and cascading-error risks; prompt-injection is lower because no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: RD-Agent can read/write logs and uses browser/API outputs, while slim reads/writes filesystem artifacts and stdin/stdout. No direct shared channel is documented, so the only plausible bridge is manual handoff or shared files. That makes injection possible but not default, and the blast radius is limited to the exchanged artifact.
conditions: IF the operator copies RD-Agent output into slim's stdin/stdout prompt
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable artifact directory
mitigations: Keep agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of model outputs into CLI prompts
Review any shared file before passing it between agents
Use read-only mounts for RD-Agent outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to exchanged artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs, and has broad network egress plus API access. slim reads filesystem artifacts and can access container images, certificate files, and private keys. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose sensitive data from RD-Agent to slim, and slim's egress can move it onward; mitigations exist but are not default.
conditions: IF RD-Agent outputs are stored in a directory slim can read
IF slim is run against artifacts containing secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Redact logs before handing them to slim
Restrict slim to a minimal input directory
Block outbound network for slim during analysis
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent supports multiple instances and broad egress; slim can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, read/write the filesystem, and modify container artifacts. Even though slim does not modify git state and RD-Agent's write surface is only logs, overlapping write access to shared files or images can still cause conflicts in default multi-agent workflows.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF slim is allowed to mutate container artifacts that RD-Agent also consumes
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Run one agent at a time on shared artifacts
Mount shared inputs read-only
Snapshot files before handing them to the other agent
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent produces research outputs and logs that slim can ingest as filesystem artifacts. slim is an interactive CLI that executes commands, so if it treats RD-Agent output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect container changes or analysis decisions. The pathway is plausible in default handoff workflows, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF slim consumes RD-Agent-generated files without verification
IF RD-Agent outputs are used as inputs to slim's command execution workflow
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents
Validate RD-Agent outputs against source data
Use checksums for transferred artifacts
Limit slim to read-only analysis mode
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff files

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent handles financial reports and logs, while slim touches certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and sensitive-data handling if the same regulated artifacts are passed between them. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch, so the concern is policy/retention rather than jurisdiction.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is passed from RD-Agent into slim
IF certificate keys or registry credentials are stored in slim-accessible artifacts
mitigations: Exclude secrets from shared inputs
Shorten retention on transferred artifacts
Mask financial fields before analysis
Restrict access to credential-bearing files
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy
